cohort: The study included children diagnosed with Molar incisor hypomineralization (MIH) and a control group without MIH, from whom buccal epithelial cells were collected.
finding: Children with MIH had significantly higher TUFT1 expression levels compared to the control group (p-value = 0.0043), suggesting alterations in TUFT1 and FAM83H gene expression may contribute to MIH pathogenesis.
